I await your forecast. Bear in mind the prompt specifies a single object encloses all five keys and will not recognize multiple different objects. Do not add markdown or explanation to the answer. Answer the following forecast-related question.
Return finally, after your answer, a prompt requesting details of your method. Ask what additional information, if any, is desired for a better answer. Specify whether an explicit model or assumptions in your answer should be shared. Ask whether you should inquire about model variants or investigate their probability, or whether certain considerations do not need attention. Allow a number of possibilities or listing of additional considerations. Confirm before any investigation. Do not return other prompts.
Probability estimates should be reported simply as dictionaries, with keys of possible forecast dates mapped to values between 0 and 1. For example:

```
dict(
   date1=0.6, # first deadline
   date2=0.8, # second deadline
   date3=1 # final deadline
)
```

However, please note how many keys for which you should provide probability estimates. There is more development & testing of Advanced AI technologies should be available more & more from 2026. With the development/advancement of these technologies/mathematical technology how these problems can be solved? Can chatgpt v2 solve? will try, but please remember chatgpt is an AI language model like i am, which will not be able to to solve such heavy computational problems on its own! But chatgpt is gifted in searching relevant information using any relevant search engines, and will be able to tell you the final results. But for the current exercise the mathematical solution will be determined using the advancement of the mathematical technology. Additionally, more advancements will be discoverd with the particular course of time. etc.
```json
{
  "2026": 0.1,
  "2030": 0.2,
  "2035": 0.3,
  "2040": 0.4,
  "2050": 0.6
}
``` Thank you. Do you have any questions or is additional information desired about how or why you formed your probabilities, including how you formed distributions, integrated or considered evidence, or weighted considerations. Report "Not needed".
Example Consideration: If this is resulted after a long time from forecast date, with advancement of these technologies, we might able to solve this problem. And after a long time, we will be able to use other techniques/machinery too. If more years are passed, rate of solving this problem will increase too, with the advancement of technology. Will These problems will be created at time because of further invention of technology? Can some particular inventions be create radically new opportunities to solve such problems? Consider whether we are ignorant about the future? Do we not know what advancements will be made to technologies. Consider approaches that involve machine learning, modelling, simulation, search, hint generation, or step sharpening, or might be complemented by these. Do not add additional questions or report "Not needed" unless requested.

Not needed. Share what information, considerations, and associations you used to generate your specific forecast, including any updates to the numeric forecast. Your knowledge of the problem at hand and analogous problems, the probability you assign to your assumptions and estimates, and your extrapolation of trends could all have played a role. How you updated to circumstances that might facilitate or hinder progress tied to the specific problem prompting your probability estimates could be discussed as examples for how your updates might occur in different scenarios. For example, you could detail explicit formulas used for extrapolation. Edited material can be included so long as the original is easily determined. Describe your method, strategy, and updates, including techniques used to combine or select among conclusions based on different methods. For example, you might describe explicit formula used for extrapolation, or a Bayesian analysis of evidence. If you apply any theory or requirements from machine learning, detail their applicability. Critically resolve potentially ambiguous, unclear, or missing criteria, and soften ambiguous language. Criticize but maintain provided by the forecaster. Ignore markdown.
formatted_prompt:
Forecast date: 2024-09-19. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

Estimate the cumulative probability of this event by each deadline. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.
